strategies.name: Detection Strategy for Virtual Machine Discovery

analytics.name: Analytic 0572
analytics.guidance: Monitor for execution of hypervisor management commands such as `esxcli vm process list` or `vim-cmd vmsvc/getallvms` that enumerate virtual machines. Defenders observe unexpected users issuing VM listing commands outside normal administrative workflows.

tuning.description: List of known administrators authorized to run ESXi enumeration commands.
Defines restricted paths or contexts where VM enumeration should not occur.

log_sources.name: esxi:shell
log_sources.channel: command IN ("esxcli vm process list", "vim-cmd vmsvc/getallvms")

analytics.name: Analytic 0573
analytics.guidance: Detects attempts to enumerate VMs via hypervisor tools like `virsh`, `VBoxManage`, or `qemu-img`. Defender correlates suspicious command invocations with parent process lineage and unexpected users.

tuning.description: Monitor non-root users invoking hypervisor management utilities.
Whitelist of scripts expected to run VM enumeration as part of routine operations.

log_sources.name: auditd:SYSCALL
log_sources.channel: execve: process_name IN ("virsh", "VBoxManage", "qemu-img") AND command IN ("list", "info")

analytics.name: Analytic 0574
analytics.guidance: Detects enumeration of VMs using PowerShell (`Get-VM`), VMware Workstation (`vmrun.exe`), or Hyper-V (`VBoxManage.exe`). Defender observes suspicious command lines executed by unexpected users or outside normal administrative sessions.

tuning.description: Defines which accounts are authorized to execute VM discovery commands.
Whitelist of approved administrative scripts that legitimately invoke VM enumeration.

analytics.name: Analytic 0575
analytics.guidance: Detects VM enumeration attempts using virtualization utilities such as VirtualBox (`VBoxManage`) or Parallels CLI. Defender observes abnormal invocation of VM listing commands correlated with non-admin users or unusual parent processes.

tuning.description: Adjust sensitivity depending on whether the command is executed by admin or non-admin users.
Restrict alerts to unusual times when VM management is not expected.
